items.title: NST Leader: Making Sarawak's Flying Doctor Service safer
items.summary: This makes the Flying Doctor Service remarkable. The entire rural healthcare delivery system needs to be reexamined. The Flying Doctor Service, introduced in 1973 to deliver healthcare to indigenous and rural communities, provides general treatment, maternal and child healthcare and childhood immunisations.

items.title: Trump says US has tools to keep AI safe, concerns are part of 'sick conspiracy'
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said on Monday that the United States already has guardrails in place to regulate and prosecute AI companies, appearing to play down concerns expressed by industry leaders over the weekend about misuse of artificial intelligence. Trump said the tools intended to keep AI safe had already been used on Amodei. Trump has resisted stirring concerns about AI and has largely embraced AI firms in his second term.

items.title: Cat-astrophe averted: Public help scoop three tonnes of 'ikan keli' off the road
items.summary: The fish, which were being transported to a newly opened fishing pond near Pelagat for a fishing competition scheduled on Sept 19, were strewn across the road after the lorry carrying them hit a road hump. Hamimi Shahira Nor Sanadi, 29, the sister-in-law of the fish supplier, said kind-hearted members of the public helped collect the fish and returned them to the lorry driver. "The impact caused the lorry's rear gate to break, and the fish spilt onto the road.

items.title: Anwar heads to Maldives after BRICS summit, India engagements
items.summary: KERALAM : Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim departed Keralam for an official visit to the Maldives today after completing his five‑day working visit to India. The aircraft carrying the Prime Minister left Calicut International Airport at 7.26pm local time (9.56pm Malaysian time) for Velana International Airport in Male. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, is accompanied by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.

items.title: Anwar's Kishore Kumar rendition goes viral as BRICS visit boosts diplomatic, economic ties
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's rendition of Kishore Kumar's classic "Khwab Ho Tum Ya Koi Haqeeqat" went viral in India, adding a soft‑diplomacy touch to his participation in the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit. The cultural gesture highlighted Malaysia–India ties while Anwar's summit focus remained on strengthening diplomacy, investment and economic cooperation. SOFT DIPLOMACY The viral moment underscored Anwar's distinctive soft diplomacy.

items.title: Anwar: BRICS not against other blocs, Malaysia pushing for fairer global order
items.summary: KERALAM : Malaysia's participation in the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit is not aimed at opposing any bloc but at advocating a fairer international system and rules, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar said Malaysia must maintain good bilateral relations with the US but should not be prevented from voicing views important for Malaysia, the region and the world. Malaysia has been a BRICS partner country since Jan 1, 2025.

items.title: Missed out? Expired plate numbers could be back on the market
items.summary: RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the initiative would cover registration numbers which had previously been successfully bid for or sold but were not registered to a vehicle within the stipulated period. He said registration numbers generally came with a specified validity period, including six or 12 months depending on the approval, within which they must be registered to a vehicle. Aedy said the prices of the re-offered numbers would not be based on their previous winning bid prices.

items.title: Anwar: Najib pardon decision guided by law, Constitution and due process
items.summary: KERALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim says the deferment of former premier Datuk Seri Najib Razak's pardon petition was made based on the rule of law, constitutional principles and official advice. He said his role in the Pardons Board meeting was subject to law and guidance from the Attorney General. "A prime minister must give views based on the law, advice from the Attorney General and the rules.

items.title: Anwar: Moderate approach on Umno issue needed to keep unity government stable
items.summary: KERALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim says he has chosen a moderate approach in handling differing views on cooperation with Umno within the unity government to ensure stability. Anwar, who is also Pakatan Harapan chairman, stressed that harsh actions could harm the country. Anwar was commenting on issues raised at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.– BERNAMA © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Two 12-year-old boys die after falling into drain in Kulim
items.summary: KULIM: Two 12-year-old boys were killed after falling into a drain, while two others were injured in an incident at Taman Desa Kayangan, Sungai Karangan, here tonight. The two injured children, aged eight and 11, were taken to hospital following the incident at 7.30pm. Kulim district police chief Superintendent Syamsul Sinring confirmed the incident, according to BuletinTV3.

items.title: 500 green sea turtle hatchlings released in Terengganu
items.summary: KERTIH: A total of 500 one-day-old green sea turtle hatchlings, each measuring 2.5cm, were released into the sea at the Ma' Daerah Turtle Sanctuary Centre in Kertih here today. Regent of Terengganu Tengku Muhammad Ismail Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin also released several turtle hatchlings at about 6.30pm. Tengku Puteri Daulath Raja Tengku Fatimatuz Zahra', Tengku Muhammad Ismail's sister, was also in attendance.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines -September 14, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Here are today's biggest stories: Jamil Khir charged Ex‑minister Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom was charged with three counts of causing Tabung Haji to dispose of RM860.3 million in assets between 2015–2017. Pas seeks answers Pas demanded an explanation from the government over the deferment of Datuk Seri Najib Razak's pardon application, calling it a matter of public interest. Police probe claim Police opened an investigation into MB Ismail Lasim's claim he was forced to sign a proclamation seeking the Negri Sembilan ruler's removal.

items.title: [UPDATED] RTD launches 'H' special registration number series for Malaysia Day
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The letter "H", which the Road Transport Department (RTD) associates with harmony, has been launched as a Special Registration Number series for Malaysia Day on Sept 16. The announcement was made by RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli at the launch of the Special Registration Number series in conjunction with Malaysia Day 2026 at Menara 118 here today. Aedy said the H series was particularly significant as the single-letter registration prefix had never previously been offered by the department.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Monday, September 14, 2026

items.title: Foong family seeks Hexza MGO exemption
items.summary: This is because the company's proposed dividend reinvestment could push their collective stake above the takeover threshold. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Hexza said the exemption is required because the shareholders intend to reinvest their final dividend entitlement into new shares. The Foong family currently holds 67.72 million shares, or 32.94 per cent of Hexza, including a 30.62 per cent stake held through Summit Holdings.

items.title: Factory bus crashes into drain in Penang, driver injured [WATCH]
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A factory bus driver was injured after the vehicle crashed through a road divider and plunged into a three-metre-deep drain. Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director John Sagun Francis said the 49-year-old driver was trapped in the bus when firefighters arrived at the scene near the Jalan Tun Dr Awang roundabout at 6.11pm. "The victim was trapped inside the bus and was successfully extricated," he said.

items.title: BMS Holdings eyes northern state expansion with Penang partner
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: BMS Holdings Bhd is proposing to form a 60:40 joint venture (JV) with the shareholders of Penang-based Wee Tatt Traders Sdn Bhd to expand its tile and building materials distribution network in northern states. In a filing to Bursa Malaysia, BMS said it signed a letter of intent with Wee Tatt shareholders Tan Kar Seng, Tan Hooi Ling and Chiew Bee Hong for the proposed JV. The JV company will be known as Jubin BMS (Wee Tatt) Sdn Bhd or another name approved by the Companies Commission of Malaysia.

items.title: Oil prices continue surge, rising 3pct amid Saudi pipeline outage after attack
items.summary: Brent crude futures climbed US$3, or 2.9 per cent, to US$107.61 a barrel by 1112 GMT, after earlier hitting a session high of US$108.65. WTI futures gained US$2.48, or 2.5 per cent, to US$102.53 a barrel. The rally pushed US diesel prices above US$6 a gallon for the first time, prompting US President Donald Trump to urge Ukraine to stop attacking Russian diesel infrastructure.

items.title: [UPDATED] Remand extended for 5 held over forged vehicle transfer documents
items.summary: IPOH: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has obtained a four-day remand extension for five people believed to have acted as middlemen for a syndicate that falsified vehicle ownership transfer documents and allegedly bribed enforcement officers in Perak. Perak MACC director Datuk Azizul Ahmad Sarkawi confirmed the extension when contacted. The suspects allegedly conspired to submit falsified documents to the RTD for vehicle ownership transfers involving 16 registration numbers.

items.title: Malaysia stronger today after major fiscal reforms – SC chairman
items.summary: Mohammad Faiz said efforts to improve the vibrancy and growth of Malaysia's capital market were being undertaken under the Capital Market Masterplan 2026-2030 (CMP), including through initiatives such as MY Value Up with Bursa Malaysia involving the country's top 88 public-listed companies. Mohammad Faiz also said Asean regulators had agreed last year on five key initiatives, including pursuing consistent voluntary carbon market standards and implementing the Asean Taxonomy Version 4. He said the Asean Capital Markets Forum (ACMF) Action Plan 2026-2030 comprised five strategic thrusts, 11 key priorities and 18 initiatives aimed at strengthening regional integration and Asean's global positioning.

items.title: Quarry worker killed when boulder falls onto lorry in Ipoh [WATCH]
items.summary: IPOH: A 53-year-old quarry worker was killed when a boulder fell onto the lorry he was driving at a quarry in Keramat Pulai here today. The victim, identified as M. Sivakumar, was trapped in the lorry following the incident at the quarry in Keramat Pulai, Kampung Kepayang. He said firefighters used hydraulic equipment to extricate the victim.

items.title: More than 20 Thai senators accused of vote-buying
items.summary: BANGKOK: Thailand's Election Commission accused 26 sitting senators on Monday of colluding to rig the last Senate election, an alleged vote-buying scandal that has sparked protests and could see them jailed. The commission said it will refer the case, which allegedly involves senators allied with Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul's party, to the Supreme Court. The 26 were among 77 people accused in the scandal, alongside 36 unsuccessful Senate candidates and 15 other political figures accused of election fraud.

items.title: Penang deploys vehicle with crane to remove abandoned cars
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A special vehicle is helping the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) remove abandoned vehicles that conventional tow trucks cannot handle. MBPP mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the "multi purpose loader with crane" was acquired in 2022 and was mainly used for abandoned where conventional tow trucks were not practical. Her post drew positive reactions, with users praising MBPP's efforts to deal with abandoned vehicles.

items.title: Croatian climber who scaled Mount Kinabalu illegally may face fine
items.summary: Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said Sabah Parks had lodged a police report over the incident involving the 46-year-old Mauro Persic, who is still in recovery. Last week, it was reported that a total of 43 search and rescue (SAR) personnel successfully brought Persic down after a five-day operation that also involved challenging terrain and rainy weather conditions. The rescue operation involved personnel from the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM); the Special Tactical Operation and Rescue Malaysia (STORM) and Mountain Search and Rescue (MOCSAR) team, as well as mountain guides, porters, rangers and other security agencies.

items.title: Croatian climber who sparked 43-man Kinabalu rescue faces action
items.summary: Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said Sabah Parks had lodged a police report over the incident involving Mauro Persic, 46, who is still receiving treatment. He said the police and Sabah Parks were investigating the case to determine further action against the tourist after he recovers. "The police and Sabah Parks are investigating the case and looking into what action should be taken.

items.title: Sabah mulls relocation of Kota Kinabalu central market
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 14 — The Sabah government is mulling three new spots for the relocation of the Kota Kinabalu central market from the heart of the city. “The government will consider and decide which site is suitable for us to build the new Kota Kinabalu central market,” he told reporters after visiting the site. Hajiji said the proposed new market was envisaged as more than a conventional public market, with various activities and facilities incorporated into the development like both dry market and wet market, a cultural, local and tourism products centre, hawkers centre and fish wharf.

items.title: US blocks Iran nuclear chief from Vienna meeting
items.summary: VIENNA: Iran's nuclear chief was blocked from attending an annual conference on Monday at the headquarters of the UN's nuclear agency in Vienna after US pressure, both Washington and Teheran said. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright confirmed to reporters that Washington had applied pressure to stop Mohammad Eslami from entering Austria, saying "he's a sanctioned individual and we don't want sanctioned individuals evading their sanctions." Behrouz Kamalvandi, a senior official from Iran's nuclear agency, accused the US of "bullying political pressure" and said the block set a precedent that would affect everybody.

items.title: Father remanded over alleged assault of daughter at Kota Baru eatery
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Police have detained a man in his 40s who allegedly kicked his daughter at an eatery in Telipot here. Kota Baru district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Azmir Damiri said the suspect surrendered himself at the Kota Baru police station yesterday and was subsequently remanded to facilitate investigations. Police had earlier sought the man and his daughter to assist investigations after a video showing him allegedly kicking the girl went viral on social media platform Threads.

items.title: Nuenergy to invest 21MWp solar PV facilities across 49 rooftop sites
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Nuenergy Holdings Bhd will invest in developing 21 megawatt-peak (MWp) solar photovoltaic (PV) facilities across 49 rooftop sites at a government agency's premises. Nuenergy said its wholly owned subsidiary IL Energy Sdn Bhd would undertake the investment, with the facilities forming part of the group's portfolio of owned renewable energy assets. The group said its other wholly owned unit Armani Sinar Sdn Bhd accepted a letter of award from the government agency on Sept 11, 2026, to collaborate as a strategic partner for the EPCC development of the facilities.

items.title: DSR Taiko, PKNP ink Mou to authenticate, certify Pahang Musang King
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: DSR Taiko Bhd plans to collaborate with the Pahang State Development Corporation (PKNP) to establish a verified origin standard and digitising export traceability for Musang King durians originating from Pahang. "The areas of collaboration under the MoU include origin authentication, labelling, traceability, certification, market development, as well as the development and promotion of 'Pahang First'," it said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia today. DSR Taiko said the initiative would form part of the proposed Pahang Durian City (PDC), which is envisaged as a strategic research and development hub for Pahang's Musang King durian.

items.title: Sabah leaders call for apology from Umno man’s remarks on Christianity
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 14 — Two Sabah leaders have called on Sepang Umno chief Datuk Noorazli Said to apologise over his controversial remarks concerning christianity and the Bible at the recent Umno general assembly. Tenom MP Datuk Arthur Kurup said Noorazli’s remarks were “highly inappropriate” and did not reflect the maturity expected of a political leader, while Tuaran MP and Tamparuli assemblyman Datuk Wilfred Madius Tangau described the joke as “grossly inappropriate and offensive”. Kurup, in a statement, said political differences did not give anyone the licence to make light of another person’s religion and beliefs for the sake of laughter or applause.

items.title: Nepal mission over, Smart team members in good health
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart), which participated in the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) mission in Nepal, arrived safely in the country at 2am today. Smart commander Senior Fire Superintendent Abdul Manaf Che Isa said the team departed from Kathmandu at 3pm yesterday (local time) aboard a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) A400M aircraft, making a brief stopover in Kolkata, India, for refueling. The Smart MAS01 team participating in the HADR mission arrived in the country via Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, on Sept 5, bringing with them 12.4 tonnes of search and rescue (SAR) equipment.

items.title: Ringgit ends higher against most major, Asean currencies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit appreciated against most major and Asean currencies at Monday's close, although it declined against the US dollar. This fluctuation occurred amid rising Brent crude prices, as markets anticipated the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) and Bank of Japan (BOJ) meetings, said an analyst. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Brent crude oil prices are currently hovering at around US$107 per barrel, adding to inflationary pressures as markets brace for the upcoming FOMC and BOJ interest rate decisions.

items.title: MACC officer denies key witness against Muhyiddin given ‘special treatment’, ‘immunity’ from own corruption case
items.summary: Under cross-examination by Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik, Mazery confirmed that Azman was a suspect in an MACC investigation in 2023 involving serious allegations of him and his associated companies KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and Addeen Engineering Sdn Bhd soliciting and accepting bribes. While confirming investigations showed Azman’s companies receiving RM9.35 million from Jana Wibawa contractors, Mazery disagreed that there is a “prima facie” case that Azman had solicited and received bribes. Mazery disagreed that his investigation on Azman is “biased”, and also denied protecting Azman.

items.title: Toy-ing with the bomb squad? Suspicious object in Sri Petaling destroyed, found to contain toy blocks (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — A suspicious plastic box found unattended in front of a shoplot in Bandar Baru Sri Petaling earlier today contained toy building blocks after a police bomb disposal unit was called to the scene. Kuala Lumpur police chief Commissioner Datuk Fadil Marsus said authorities were alerted to the box at about 12.57pm after a 33-year-old woman reported the discovery. “Initial checks found that the object had a high radiation reading, which prompted the deployment of a Bomb Disposal Unit, together with the Bukit Aman Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear and Explosive (CBRNE) Unit, to the scene for further checks and evaluation,” he said.

items.title: Haze update: 22 areas register unhealthy air quality at 4pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — A total of 22 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 4pm today. According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, four areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Serian (181), Sri Aman (166), Samarahan (153) and Kuching (152). Forty-five areas had a moderate API reading while only Kangar in Perlis had a good API reading.

items.title: Ex-director faces 71 cheating charges over RM4.7m used car scam
items.summary: He was accused of cheating Wong Yoong Jed, a director of Viso Capital Sdn Bhd and Lio Capital Sdn Bhd, by deceiving him into believing that various vehicles had been purchased. This induced Wong to transfer RM1.69 million from Lio Capital and Viso Capital into Buycar2u’s bank account. Before Judges Norma and Muhammad Ilmami, the accused faced 30 charges involving RM1.98 million and 15 charges involving RM1.02 million, respectively.

items.title: Transport minister: Private vehicle ownership transfer inspection fees will remain standardised, no price competition
items.summary: SUNGAI BULOH, Sept 14 — The multi-operator system for motor vehicle inspection services does not allow licensed operators to compete on price, but requires them to focus on the efficiency and quality of their services, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke. He said the fee for private vehicle ownership transfer inspections (M.V.15) will remain standardised and regulated by the government through the Road Transport Department (JPJ) at all licensed centres. On operational efficiency, Loke said the inspection process at licensed private centres takes less than 20 minutes when conducted according to the prescribed schedule, adding that the results are transmitted directly to the JPJ system, facilitating the vehicle ownership transfer process.

items.title: Carried by teenager porter, rescued Croatian climber says Kinabalu ordeal broke his heart
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 14 — Croatian climber Mauro Persic has expressed regret over the risks he took after being found injured and alone on Mount Kinabalu for eight days, but said the ordeal strengthened his faith in human compassion. Persic, 46, said the rescue operation was a humbling experience, particularly when rescuers and porters had to carry him down because he was too weak and injured to continue on his own, Berita Harian reported. 40 people risking their lives to save one.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution: Second multi-purpose mission ship under construction in Turkiye to be completed by end‑2027
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — The second Multi-Purpose Mission Ship (MPMS), which is currently under construction in Turkiye, is expected to be completed and handed over to the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) by the end of next year, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the first MPMS vessel was expected to arrive in March next year, a month before the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA). Saifuddin Nasution said he would travel to Istanbul, Turkiye, at the end of this month to personally inspect the progress of the vessel’s construction.

items.title: Anthony Loke calls for Pakatan Presidential Council meeting to discuss recent political developments after Umno assembly
items.summary: SUNGAI BULOH, Sept 14 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said he will propose to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim that the Pakatan Harapan (PH) Presidential Council convene to discuss recent political developments following statements made at the Umno General Assembly. He said the recent statements raised concerns regarding political certainty and stability, which could affect investor and public confidence in the country. The Prime Minister must also make this clear with all component parties,” the Transport Minister said.

items.title: Penang Port Commission, PPSB to offer free ferry services on Malaysia Day
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — The Penang Port Commission (SPPP) and Penang Port Sdn Bhd (PPSB) are offering free ferry services to Malaysians on September 16 in conjunction with Malaysia Day celebrations and the Keretapi Sarong Festival. SPPP chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said the offer applies to trips from both ferry terminals, Pangkalan Sultan Abdul Halim (PSAH) in Seberang Perai and Pangkalan Raja Tun Uda (PRTU) here, in accordance with the existing service schedule. According to him, during last year’s Malaysia Day celebration, a total of 10,094 pedestrians and 1,909 two-wheeled vehicles utilised the ferry service for round trips.

items.title: Chief of Defence Force: MAF proposes reinstating multi‑agency border‑security framework used under former national task force
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) has submitted a proposal to the National Security Council (NSC) to reinstate a multi-agency operational framework modelled on the National Task Force (NTF) to bolster national border security. Chief of Defence Force Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the proposal, submitted through the National Operational Management Committee, would bring together various agencies including the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA), the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM), and the Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM). He said the strategic coordination of enforcement agencies has proven more effective in addressing security vulnerabilities along the country’s land and maritime borders.

items.title: Two‑year‑old mauled by stray dogs in Batu Pahat to undergo reconstructive surgery
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Sept 14 — A two-year-old girl mauled by stray dogs outside her grandmother’s home in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, is expected to undergo reconstructive surgery soon as she continues to fight for her life. Nur Haira Wafiqah Mohammad Hamizi was critically injured in the Sept 6 attack by five dogs, suffering severe head and facial wounds. Previously, the authorities caught seven dogs, including five puppies, which attacked Haira.

items.title: Free entry to three Penang heritage sites for two days starting tomorrow in conjunction with Malaysia Day
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — Three heritage sites in Penang will offer free entry for two days from tomorrow in conjunction with the fifth anniversary of Penang Hill’s recognition as a Unesco Biosphere Reserve and Malaysia Day. State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the three sites are the Penang State Automotive Gallery, Fort Cornwallis and the Penang State Museum. “The public and tourists from Malaysia and abroad, are welcome to take this opportunity to explore history, appreciate the state’s heritage, gain a deeper understanding of Penang’s past and discover Malaysia’s rich and diverse cultural heritage,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Federal Court hears PKR’s argument that Zuraida’s RM10m bond was reasonable; decision reserved
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — The Federal Court was told today that the High Court’s decision ordering former Ampang MP Datuk Zuraida Kamaruddin to pay RM10 million to Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) for breaching a bond with the party was reasonable. “Zuraida admitted that the value conferred upon her exceeded RM10 million, while the operative clause fixed RM10 million as the sum payable upon the occurrence of the stipulated events,” he said during PKR’s appeal against a Court of Appeal decision reducing the bond payment from RM10 million to RM100,000. “The recital recorded Zuraida’s admission that the value conferred upon her exceeded RM10 million.

items.title: New Lawas Hospital expected to evolve into specialist centre to cut long‑distance referrals, says deputy health minister
items.summary: LAWAS, Sept 14 — The new 76-bed Lawas Hospital is expected to evolve into a specialist hospital, thereby reducing the local population’s reliance on distant hospitals. “I hope that God willing, medical specialists will be permanently based at Lawas Hospital, rather than relying on scheduled visiting specialists. I hope this facility will become a specialist hospital,” she said at the Lawas Hospital project handover ceremony here today.

items.title: Abdul Aziz appointed Deputy Inspector‑General of Police
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Management Director Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid has been appointed Deputy Inspector-General of Police, effective September 9. He joined the PDRM on July 1, 1995, and has served in various departments throughout his career, including the Management Department, Special Branch, Criminal Investigation Department, Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department, Commercial Crime Investigation Department, Logistics and Technology Department, and Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department. Abdul Aziz has held several key positions, including Management Director, Deputy Director of Special Branch, Deputy Director of Narcotics, Penang Police Deputy Chief, Principal Assistant Director of Management Policy/Human Resource, and Principal Assistant Director of the Special Integrated Investigation Team.

items.title: Court of Appeal slashes Muhammad Shafee’s damages in Malaysian Bar suit to RM120,000
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — The Court of Appeal today reduced the damages awarded to senior lawyer Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah from RM340,000 to RM120,000 in his suit against the Malaysian Bar and two others for breach of statutory duty. The bench also dismissed Muhammad Shafee’s appeal seeking an increase in the quantum of damages. On May 26, 2016, the High Court dismissed Muhammad Shafee’s suit.

items.title: Sixteen drownings in Pahang this year, Bomba urges public to respect warning signs
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 14 — A total of 16 drowning deaths have been recorded in Pahang so far this year, and the public is urged to prioritise safety when engaging in activities near rivers, waterfalls, and beaches. Pahang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations and rescue, Mohd Salahuddin Isa, said key safety measures include heeding warning signs and refraining from swimming in areas identified as dangerous. “To date, 16 drowning cases resulting in 16 deaths have been recorded across the state; we advise the public to always prioritise safety and understand the risks associated with recreational areas.

items.title: Home minister confirms police investigating Negeri Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim’s duress claim
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — Police have opened an investigation paper into Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim’s claim that he signed an instrument of proclamation with regard to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar against his will and under duress. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said further developments would be shared if there was progress in the investigation. “The investigation paper has been opened and is still in progress.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng dares Zahid, demands Penang Pakatan expel Umno and defer hikes
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — DAP’s Air Putih assemblyman Lim Guan Eng has questioned why Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi dared the Pakatan Harapan-led federal government to expel Umno from Putrajaya, but did not issue the same challenge to Penang’s PH administration. Lim noted that Umno holds positions in the Penang state executive council, both city councils and state linked companies. He suggested Zahid lacked the courage to push Penang PH because the coalition would still retain a two thirds majority in the state assembly even without Umno’s two elected representatives.

items.title: Najib pardon delay not automatic, PAS claims objections triggered deferral
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — PAS has called on the government to explain why the Federal Territories Pardons Board deferred consideration of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s application for a royal pardon. PAS secretary general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the matter was of public interest and should not be withheld from the people. “PAS demands that the government immediately clarify this issue to the public,” he added.

items.title: High Court acquits 15‑year‑old of Bandar Utama school murder, rules unsound mind
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 14 — The High Court today acquitted and discharged a 15-year-old boy of the charge of murdering a female student at a secondary school in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, last year. Speaking to reporters outside the court, the teenager’s lawyer Kitson Foong said the court held that his client was of unsound mind at the time of the incident. The teenager’s lawyer Kitson Foong said the court held that his client was of unsound mind at the time of the incident.

items.title: Bintulu Port comes under Sarawak jurisdiction following repeal of federal Acts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — Bintulu Port has officially transitioned from a federal port to a state port under the jurisdiction of the Sarawak government, effective September 1, 2026. Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd (BPHB) said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia that the transition follows the enactment of two acts — the Declaration of an Area in the Bintulu District to be a Federal Port (Repeal) Act 2024 [Act 858] and the Bintulu Port Authority (Dissolution) Act 2024 [Act 859]. It said Bintulu Port Sdn Bhd’s (BPSB) operation, management and development of Bintulu Port are governed by the heads of agreement dated July 27, 2026, entered into between the Sarawak government, Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak) (BPA Sarawak) and BPSB, pending the execution of the Port Operation Concession Agreement (POCA).

items.title: Fahmi warns that communalism and corruption can weaken Malaysia’s future
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 14 — Malaysia’s younger generation must understand the country’s history and appreciate the struggles of previous generations in building a peaceful and united nation, while rejecting corruption that could undermine the country’s future. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said there were three things that could destroy a country, namely communism, communalism and corruption. He said communism had once posed a major threat to national security, with armed movements, killings and disruptions to public peace capable of undermining Malaysia’s stability.

items.title: KM263.6 southbound towards Menora Tunnel now safe for motorists after rapid slope‑erosion mitigation, says Perak exco
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 14 — The state government has assured that the North-South Expressway (PLUS) route near KM263.6, southbound towards the Meru-Ipoh Utara (Menora) Tunnel, is now safe after the area experienced slope erosion on Sept 11. Perak Infrastructure, Energy, Water and Transport Committee chairman Datuk Seri Mohammad Nizar Jamaluddin said that authorities have carried out immediate and continuous monitoring, along with mitigation measures, to ensure traffic safety at all times. On long-term safety measures, Mohammad Nizar said PLUS is currently drafting proposals for slope structure reinforcement as well as the installation of steel netting in high-risk areas.

items.title: Fire Dept working with Public Service Dept to ensure welfare of two officers missing in Nepal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — The Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) will ensure that the welfare of its two officers who remain uncontactable following flash floods in Rasuwa, Nepal last month is taken care of. Its director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the department had consulted the Public Service Department (PSD) on matters relating to the two officers’ salaries and pensions. He said checks showed that JBPM headquarters deputy director of the Planning and Research Division Mohd Sani Harul is due to retire on September 23, while its Central Region Academy officer Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa still has many years of service remaining.

items.title: MAF ready to support emergency flying doctor service evacuations, says Chief of Defence Forces
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) is ready to deploy its air assets to assist the Health Ministry (MoH) in providing Flying Doctor Service (FDS), particularly for emergency medical evacuations in remote areas. Chief of Defence Forces Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the move was aimed at meeting the ministry’s urgent needs following last Tuesday’s FDS helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak. Yesterday, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said four government agencies, including the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), would assist the MoH in providing temporary mercy flights.

items.title: MOF tours states to gather Budget 2027 input from industries, NGOs and public, says Amir Hamzah
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — The Ministry of Finance (MOF) is conducting a budget tour to gather views and suggestions from industry players, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and members of the public nationwide as it prepares for Budget 2027. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the tour aims to gain insight into the needs of key sectors in each state and obtain input from parties directly affected by government policies and allocations. Amir Hamzah said Penang is among the locations due to its important role in the electrical and electronics (E&E) and semiconductor sectors.
